entities.summary: The first generation of trams in Luxembourg City ran from 1875 to 1964, before they were withdrawn from service and the tramways removed. A second generation of trams began operational service in December 2017, along a new route, completed in March 2025, that runs from Luxembourg Airport in the north-east to the Cloche d'Or business district in Gasperich in the south, serving the new national stadium, via Howald, Pfaffenthal-Kirchberg and Luxembourg railway stations. Additional lines are planned for the network both within Luxembourg City, as well as extending to Strassen and Esch-sur-Alzette.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Luxemburg tramway museum matters as it preserves a piece of Luxembourg's transportation history and provides a unique educational resource for future generations. The modern tram network has also had a positive impact on the city's economy and environmental sustainability.
